name: Fused connection unit plan mark
summary: Plan mark for a fused connection unit that feeds fixed equipment through a cartridge fuse instead of a plug.
description: A fused connection unit, often called a fused spur, connects a fixed appliance such as a towel rail, extractor fan or boiler directly to a final circuit through a small cartridge fuse. Plans commonly draw a small square with an S-shaped fuse mark or the letters FCU at the wall line, sometimes with a switch stroke for the switched type.

The symbol is common in British-style layouts on ring final circuits, where fixed loads must be fused down from the circuit rating. The reader should check the fuse rating and whether a flex outlet is fitted on the front or the cable leaves from the back of the box.
It is not a socket outlet: no plug is involved. It also does not provide isolation suitable for mechanical maintenance unless the specification says so.
readingNotes: Read the fuse rating written beside the symbol, often 3 A or 13 A.
Check whether the switched or unswitched version is required.
drawingChecklist: State fuse rating and switched or unswitched type.
Name the fixed appliance it serves.
Show the flex outlet or rear cable entry.
distinction: A switched socket outlet accepts a plug; a fused connection unit is wired to fixed equipment.
